question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

He was so enraged at the article about him that he sued the newspaper.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Angered.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enraged" means made very angry / furious. Its closest synonym is "Angered". (अत्यधिक क्रोधित)

◦ Correct: He was so enraged (angered) at the article about him that he sued the newspaper.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Generated" (produced/created), Option 2 "Determined" (resolved/decided) and Option 4 "Enhanced" (improved) are unrelated to anger.

NOTE

• Synonyms of enraged: angered, infuriated, incensed, furious, irate. Antonyms: pleased, calmed, delighted, soothed.

question:
Recognise the sentence with the correct transitive verb form of break.

A. The cyclone broke the window.  B. The window broke.  C. The cyclone caused the breaking of window.  D. The cyclone caused the broken window.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A — "The cyclone broke the window."

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A transitive verb is one that takes a direct object (it acts upon something). In sentence A, "broke" is followed by the object "the window" — "The cyclone broke the window" — so "break" is used correctly as a transitive verb.

◦ Structure: Subject (cyclone) + transitive verb (broke) + object (the window).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• In sentence B ("The window broke"), "broke" has no object — here it is intransitive, not transitive.

• Sentences C and D avoid the finite verb altogether, using the noun "breaking" or the adjective "broken", so neither shows the transitive verb "break".

NOTE

• "Break" is both transitive (He broke the glass) and intransitive (The glass broke). A transitive verb always answers "broke what?" with an object.

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

BBC Media has shown exponenteal growth in their revenue this year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. exponenteal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Exponenteal" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "exponential", meaning very rapid (growth) that increases more and more quickly. (तीव्र गति से बढ़ना)

◦ Correct: BBC Media has shown exponential growth in their revenue this year.

• Spelling key: EX + PO + NEN + TIAL.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "revenue" (income), "media" and "year" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: exponent, exponentially. "Exponential growth" describes a doubling/compounding increase (as in the powers of a number).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Leisure activities are activities that people ___________ in during their free time while they are not working.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. engage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal expression "engage in" means to take part in / be involved in an activity. So people "engage in" leisure activities during their free time. (भाग लेना)

◦ Correct: ... activities that people engage in during their free time ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "encourage" (to give support), Option 3 "evaluate" (to assess) and Option 4 "exempt" (to free from an obligation) do not collocate with "in" to give this meaning.

NOTE

• "Engage in (an activity)" = participate in it. Also note "engaged to" (to be married), "engaged with" (occupied with).

question: Select the option that has used the correct tense.
option_1: By the time we arrive at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
option_2: By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
option_3: By the time we arrives at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
option_4: By the time we arriving at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When one past action is completed before another past action, we use the past simple for the later event and the past perfect (continuous) for the earlier, longer one. "By the time we arrived (past simple) ... they had been waiting (past perfect continuous) for over an hour."

◦ Correct: By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "arrive" and Option 3 "arrives" are present-tense forms and clash with the past "had been waiting".

• Option 4 "arriving" is a non-finite form and cannot stand as the main verb of the clause.

NOTE

• Past perfect continuous = had + been + V-ing, used for an action going on up to a point in the past (had been waiting for an hour).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

It is a common perception / that the rich sometimes / despise poor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. despise poor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When an adjective denotes a class of people (rich, poor, blind, etc.), it must be preceded by "the" and functions as a plural noun. Since "the rich" is used earlier, the parallel form is "the poor", not just "poor".

◦ Correct: ... that the rich sometimes despise the poor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "It is a common perception" and "that the rich sometimes" are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• "The + adjective" = a whole class/group: the rich, the poor, the young, the elderly, the unemployed. These take a plural verb (The poor are ...).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Searing
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Freezing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Searing" means extremely hot / burning (scorching). Its antonym is "Freezing", meaning extremely cold. (झुलसा देने वाला का विलोम — अत्यधिक ठंडा)

◦ Example: The searing desert heat was the opposite of the freezing mountain air.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Mocking" (ridiculing), Option 2 "Pressing" (urgent) and Option 4 "Thrilling" (exciting) are unrelated to temperature.

NOTE

• Synonyms of searing: scorching, blistering, burning, sweltering. Antonyms: freezing, icy, frosty, chilly.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Prem is an excellent chess player. He is the _______ student of the class too.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. most intelligent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" before the blank and the phrase "of the class" (a comparison among the whole group) call for the superlative degree — "the most intelligent".

◦ Correct: He is the most intelligent student of the class too.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "more intelligent" is the comparative (used with "than", between two), which does not fit "the ... of the class".

• Option 2 "intelligently" is an adverb and Option 3 "intelligent" (positive degree) do not suit "the ... student of the class".

NOTE

• Degrees: intelligent – more intelligent (than) – the most intelligent (of/in a group). Use the superlative with "the" when comparing one with all others.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Boisterous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Quiet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Boisterous" means noisy, rowdy and full of energy. Its antonym is "Quiet", meaning calm and making little noise. (कोलाहलपूर्ण का विलोम — शांत)

◦ Example: The boisterous crowd fell quiet when the anthem began.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Noisy" is a synonym of boisterous.

• Option 2 "Benevolent" (kind) and Option 3 "Buoyant" (cheerful/floating) are unrelated antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of boisterous: noisy, rowdy, unruly, loud, exuberant. Antonyms: quiet, calm, restrained, subdued.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

The minister went to visit the monuments set up for people who were buried in other countries.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. cenotaphs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "cenotaph" is a monument (tomb-like structure) built in honour of a person or people whose remains are buried elsewhere / in another place. It exactly matches "monuments set up for people who were buried in other countries". (स्मारक — जहाँ शव कहीं और दफ़न हो)

◦ Example: The cenotaph honours soldiers buried far from home.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "graves" (holes where bodies are buried), Option 2 "cemetery" (a burial ground) and Option 4 "coffins" (boxes for a dead body) all involve the actual body, unlike a cenotaph.

NOTE

• Root: Greek "kenos" (empty) + "taphos" (tomb) → an "empty tomb". India Gate in Delhi is a famous cenotaph honouring fallen soldiers.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Sushil, who recently joined our school / was awarded the Gold Cup / as he worked hardly / throughout the year.
option_2: Sushil, who recently joined our school
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. as he worked hardly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hardly" is NOT the adverb form of "hard"; it means "scarcely / almost not". The intended meaning is that he worked with effort, for which the correct word is "hard" (which is both an adjective and an adverb).

◦ Correct: ... as he worked hard throughout the year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Sushil, who recently joined our school", "was awarded the Gold Cup" and "throughout the year" are all correct.

NOTE

• "He works hard" (with effort) vs "He hardly works" (almost never). Similar traps: late/lately, near/nearly, high/highly.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

His sudden resignation left the company in a very difficult situation and to have to make a hard decision as they scrambled to find a replacement.
option_3: between a rock and a hard place
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. between a rock and a hard place.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "between a rock and a hard place" means in a very difficult situation where one has to choose between two equally unpleasant options. It fits "a very difficult situation ... make a hard decision". (दो कठिनाइयों के बीच फँसना)

◦ Example: With both choices costly, the board was between a rock and a hard place.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "in the dark" (unaware), Option 2 "with a silver lining" (a hopeful side of a bad situation) and Option 4 "on cloud nine" (extremely happy) do not fit a difficult dilemma.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of dilemma: "caught between two stools", "in a fix", "on the horns of a dilemma", "in a tight spot".

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The weather was absolutley perfect for the outdoor event.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. absolutely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "absolutely", meaning completely / totally. (पूर्णतः)

◦ Correct: The weather was absolutely perfect for the outdoor event.

• Spelling key: AB + SO + LUTE + LY (from "absolute" + "-ly").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt: "absoultely", "absoluttley" and "absolutly" all disturb the base word "absolute".

NOTE

• To form the adverb, add "-ly" to "absolute" → keep the full base and simply attach "-ly": absolute → absolutely.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

an open book
option_1: someone who gives advice based on theory not practice
option_3: a person of whom her mother is extremely proud
option_4: a person or thing that is easy to learn about and understand
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. a person or thing that is easy to learn about and understand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "an open book" refers to a person (or thing) whose thoughts, feelings or nature are easy to know and understand — nothing is hidden. (खुली किताब — जिसे आसानी से समझा जा सके)

◦ Example: You always know how she feels; she is an open book.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 describe an armchair theorist, a helpful person and a favoured child respectively — none matches "an open book".

NOTE

• Opposite idea: "a closed book" = something/someone difficult to understand, as in "He is a closed book about his past".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Meticulous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Regardless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Meticulous" means very careful, precise and attentive to every small detail. Its antonym is "Regardless" (here meaning careless / paying no heed / without attention to detail). (सूक्ष्म/सतर्क का विलोम — लापरवाह)

◦ Example: A meticulous worker checks everything, whereas a regardless (careless) worker ignores details.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Persevering" (persistent), Option 2 "Exemplary" (model/ideal) and Option 3 "Determined" (resolute) are broadly positive and do not oppose "meticulous".

NOTE

• Synonyms of meticulous: careful, thorough, scrupulous, painstaking. Antonyms: careless, sloppy, negligent, slapdash.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

I have never seen so beautiful a landscape than this one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. than this one.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "so + adjective + a/an + noun ... as" takes "as", not "than". "Than" is used only with the comparative degree, but here there is no comparative. So it should be "as this one".

◦ Correct: I have never seen so beautiful a landscape as this one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "I have never seen", "so beautiful" and "a landscape" are all correct in this construction ("so + adjective + a + singular noun").

NOTE

• "As ... as" is used for equality/positive degree; "than" only with comparatives (bigger than, more beautiful than). "So beautiful a landscape as" is correct.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A post without any remuneration
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Honorary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Honorary" describes a post/position held without any salary or payment (remuneration) — held as an honour. (अवैतनिक / मानद पद)

◦ Example: She serves as the honorary secretary of the club, receiving no pay.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Illegible" (unable to be read), Option 2 "Bigot" (an intolerant person) and Option 3 "Effeminate" (having womanly qualities) do not relate to an unpaid post.

NOTE

• Related: "honorary degree" (given as an honour, without study). Do not confuse with "honorable" (deserving respect).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Corroborate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Support.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Corroborate" means to confirm or give supporting evidence for a statement/theory. Its closest synonym is "Support". (पुष्टि करना / समर्थन करना)

◦ Example: The witness's account corroborated (supported) the victim's story.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Suggest" (to propose), Option 3 "Contend" (to argue/assert or compete) and Option 4 "Elaborate" (to explain in detail) do not mean to confirm with evidence.

NOTE

• Synonyms of corroborate: confirm, verify, substantiate, validate, endorse. Antonyms: contradict, refute, disprove.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase.

Belonging or pertaining to an individual from birth
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Congenital.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Congenital" means existing from or present at birth (especially of a trait or a disease). It matches "belonging ... to an individual from birth". (जन्मजात)

◦ Example: A congenital heart defect is one present from birth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Congregational" (relating to a congregation/assembly), Option 3 "Congruent" (in agreement / matching) and Option 4 "Congenial" (friendly/pleasant) do not mean "from birth".

NOTE

• "Congenital" (from birth) vs "genetic" (inherited through genes) vs "hereditary" (passed from parents). Congenital conditions may or may not be inherited.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Forgetfull.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Forgetfull" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "forgetful", meaning tending to forget things. The suffix "-ful" is always written with a single 'l'. (भुलक्कड़)

◦ Correct: My grandfather has become quite forgetful.

• Spelling key: FORGET + FUL (one 'l').

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Damaged", "Fantastic" and "Expensive" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• The suffix "-ful" always has one 'l': beautiful, careful, useful, helpful, forgetful. (It doubles to "-fully" only when "-ly" is added: carefully.)

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Though people are becoming health-conscious these days, (1)________ simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases. (2)________ a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology', (3)________ food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure , and ischemic heart disease. A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated (4)________ high sodium intake. As per the research, a person's individual sodium intake over time may be predicted by how (5)____ they salt their food. It is found that people who do not put a little additional salt to their food very often had a much lower risk of heart disease event regardless of lifestyle factors and pre-existing disease.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. because of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Because of" is a prepositional phrase followed by a noun/noun phrase ("simple lifestyle habits"). It gives the reason — people fall ill because of their simple/poor lifestyle habits. (के कारण)

◦ Correct: ... because of simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "because" is a conjunction and must be followed by a clause (subject + verb), not just a noun phrase.

• Option 1 "for" and Option 4 "but" do not give the cause-and-effect link needed here.

NOTE

• "Because" + clause (because they neglect habits); "because of" + noun (because of habits). Both mean "for the reason that".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Though people are becoming health-conscious these days, (1)________ simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases. (2)________ a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology', (3)________ food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure , and ischemic heart disease. A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated (4)________ high sodium intake. As per the research, a person's individual sodium intake over time may be predicted by how (5)____ they salt their food. It is found that people who do not put a little additional salt to their food very often had a much lower risk of heart disease event regardless of lifestyle factors and pre-existing disease.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. According to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression "according to" is used to cite a source or authority ("a new study ..."). It means "as stated by". (के अनुसार)

◦ Correct: According to a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology' ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "According with", Option 3 "In according with" are ungrammatical.

• Option 2 "Accordingly" is an adverb meaning "therefore / in a corresponding way" and cannot introduce a source.

NOTE

• Remember: it is always "according to (someone/something)" — never "according with". "According to me" reports one's opinion.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Though people are becoming health-conscious these days, (1)________ simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases. (2)________ a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology', (3)________ food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure , and ischemic heart disease. A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated (4)________ high sodium intake. As per the research, a person's individual sodium intake over time may be predicted by how (5)____ they salt their food. It is found that people who do not put a little additional salt to their food very often had a much lower risk of heart disease event regardless of lifestyle factors and pre-existing disease.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. salting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a gerund (V-ing) to act as the subject of the verb "is linked". "Salting food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk ..." — the "-ing" form works as a noun (subject). (क्रिया का संज्ञा-रूप)

◦ Correct: ... salting food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "salt" (base verb) and Option 2 "salted" (past form) cannot function as the subject of the sentence.

• Option 4 "salt with" is grammatically wrong here.

NOTE

• A gerund (V-ing used as a noun) can be the subject of a sentence: "Reading is fun", "Salting food ... is linked ...". The verb that follows is singular.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Though people are becoming health-conscious these days, (1)________ simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases. (2)________ a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology', (3)________ food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure , and ischemic heart disease. A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated (4)________ high sodium intake. As per the research, a person's individual sodium intake over time may be predicted by how (5)____ they salt their food. It is found that people who do not put a little additional salt to their food very often had a much lower risk of heart disease event regardless of lifestyle factors and pre-existing disease.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "correlate" takes the preposition "with". High blood pressure is "correlated with high sodium intake" — i.e., the two are connected/associated. (के साथ संबंधित)

◦ Correct: ... high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated with high sodium intake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Prepositions "in", "of" and "for" do not collocate with "correlated" in standard usage.

NOTE

• Fixed collocations: "correlated with", "associated with", "linked to/with", "connected with/to". Note earlier the passage uses "linked to".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Though people are becoming health-conscious these days, (1)________ simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases. (2)________ a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology', (3)________ food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure , and ischemic heart disease. A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated (4)________ high sodium intake. As per the research, a person's individual sodium intake over time may be predicted by how (5)____ they salt their food. It is found that people who do not put a little additional salt to their food very often had a much lower risk of heart disease event regardless of lifestyle factors and pre-existing disease.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. frequently.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adverb of frequency to modify "they salt their food". "How frequently they salt their food" (i.e., how often) fits the context of measuring salt intake over time. (कितनी बार / अक्सर)

◦ Correct: ... may be predicted by how frequently they salt their food.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "soundly" (deeply/thoroughly, as in sleep), Option 2 "hefty" (large/heavy) and Option 3 "burly" (strong and heavily built) are adjectives/adverbs that do not describe how often something is done.

• The passage's last line ("... do not put a little additional salt ... very often") confirms the theme of frequency.

NOTE

• Adverbs of frequency: always, usually, often, frequently, sometimes, rarely, never. They tell "how often" an action happens.

question: If four resistances of 4 ohm each are connected in parallel, what will be their effective resistance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 ohm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• For resistances in parallel, the effective (equivalent) resistance is given by:

◦ 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ + 1/R₄

• With four equal resistances of 4 Ω each: 1/R = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 4/4 = 1, so R = 1 Ω. (समांतर क्रम — 1 ओम)

◦ Shortcut: for n equal resistances R in parallel, effective resistance = R/n = 4/4 = 1 Ω.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• In a parallel combination the equivalent resistance is less than the smallest individual resistance.

• In a series combination, resistances simply add up: R = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + R₄ = 16 Ω.

NOTE

• SI unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω). Ohm's law: V = IR. Parallel connections keep voltage the same across each resistor; series connections keep current the same.

question: Bhavnath Mahadev fair is held every year in which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Junagarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Bhavnath Mahadev Fair (Mela)" is held every year at the foot of Girnar Hills in Junagadh (Junagarh), Gujarat, around Maha Shivratri. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva (Bhavnath Mahadev). (भवनाथ महादेव मेला — जूनागढ़, गुजरात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The fair is famous for the gathering of Naga sadhus and a grand procession (Maha Puja) held at midnight on Maha Shivratri.

• The Girnar Hills near Junagadh are a sacred site for both Hindus and Jains.

NOTE

• Other important fairs of Gujarat: Tarnetar Fair, Vautha Fair and the Rann Utsav in the Kutch region.

question: As per the 2001 Census, what is the specific age, for a person to be called literate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India (from 1991 onwards, including 2001), a "literate" is a person aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language. (साक्षर — 7 वर्ष और उससे अधिक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A person who can only read but cannot write is not counted as literate.

• Children below 7 years are treated as illiterate by default for census purposes.

• Before 1991, the age limit used was 5 years.

NOTE

• The 2011 Census recorded India's literacy rate at about 74% (male ~82%, female ~65%). Kerala is the most literate state; Bihar the least.

question: A section of an active fault that has produced earthquakes in the past but is now quiet and is believed that the fault segment is capable of producing earthquake on some other basis is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seismic Gap.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Seismic Gap" is a segment of an active fault that has produced earthquakes in the past but is currently quiet, and is believed to be capable of producing (storing energy for) a future earthquake. (भूकंपीय अंतराल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Hypocenter (focus): the actual point inside the Earth where an earthquake originates.

• Epicenter: the point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus.

• Seismic waves: the waves (P-waves, S-waves, surface waves) that carry earthquake energy.

NOTE

• Earthquakes are measured for magnitude on the Richter scale and for intensity on the Mercalli scale; they are recorded by a seismograph.

question: When was the Wildlife Protection Act passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1972.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Wildlife (Protection) Act" was passed in 1972 to protect wild animals, birds and plants and to provide for the establishment of national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and protected areas in India. (वन्यजीव संरक्षण अधिनियम — 1972)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Under this Act, Project Tiger was launched in 1973 and Project Elephant in 1992.

• The Act provides different Schedules (I–VI) giving varying degrees of protection to species.

NOTE

• Other key environmental laws: Water Act (1974), Forest (Conservation) Act (1980), Air Act (1981) and Environment (Protection) Act (1986).

question: In July 2023, Tribhuvaneshwar Saran Singh Deo was appointed as Deputy Chief Minister of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In July 2023, Tribhuvaneshwar Saran Singh Deo (T. S. Singh Deo) was appointed as the Deputy Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh in the then Congress government led by Bhupesh Baghel. (छत्तीसगढ़ के उपमुख्यमंत्री — टी. एस. सिंह देव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000; its capital is Raipur.

• The state is rich in minerals (coal, iron ore) and forests, and is known as the "Rice Bowl of India".

NOTE

• The post of Deputy Chief Minister is not mentioned in the Constitution; it is a political arrangement, and a Deputy CM enjoys the status of a state Cabinet Minister.

question: The Mahananda River rising in the ________ is a tributary of Ganga.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Darjeeling hills.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mahananda River" rises in the Darjeeling hills (Himalayas) of West Bengal and is a left-bank tributary of the Ganga. (महानंदा नदी — दार्जिलिंग की पहाड़ियाँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Mahananda flows through West Bengal and Bihar and finally joins the Ganga.

• It should not be confused with the Mahanadi, a peninsular river of Chhattisgarh and Odisha that drains into the Bay of Bengal.

NOTE

• Major left-bank tributaries of the Ganga: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi and Mahananda. Right-bank tributaries include the Yamuna and Son.

question: Which of the following is a traditional game of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kabaddi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kabaddi" is a traditional / indigenous contact game of India, played between two teams where a "raider" tries to tag opponents and return to their half while holding their breath (traditionally chanting "kabaddi"). (कबड्डी — भारत का पारंपरिक खेल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kabaddi is the state game of several Indian states and is very popular in South Asia.

• India has dominated the Kabaddi World Cup and Asian Games Kabaddi events; the Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) has boosted its popularity.

NOTE

• Volleyball, Basketball and Football are internationally originated games. Other traditional Indian games: Kho-Kho, Gilli-Danda, Kancha and Langdi.

question: A group of natural substances with variable phenolic structures, which are found in fruits, vegetables, and grains is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Flavonoids.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Flavonoids" are a group of natural substances with variable phenolic structures, found in fruits, vegetables, grains, bark, roots, flowers, tea and wine. They are well known for their antioxidant properties. (फ्लेवोनॉइड्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Flavonoids act as plant pigments (giving colour to flowers/fruits) and help protect plants from UV rays and pathogens.

• In humans they are valued as antioxidants that help neutralise harmful free radicals.

NOTE

• Pectins are polysaccharides used as gelling agents (in jams); resins are sticky plant secretions; hopanoids are compounds in bacterial cell membranes.

question: The Moplah Uprising, an organised opposition of Muslim cultivators, occurred in which modern state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Moplah (Mappila) Uprising / Rebellion of 1921" was an organised revolt of Muslim (Mappila) cultivators against Hindu landlords (Jenmis) and British authorities in the Malabar region of present-day Kerala. (मोपला विद्रोह — केरल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The revolt was linked with the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movements and was driven by agrarian discontent among the tenant cultivators.

• Its notable leaders included Ali Musaliyar and Variyankunnath Kunjahammad Haji.

NOTE

• Other peasant/tribal revolts: Santhal Rebellion (1855), Indigo Revolt (1859), Deccan Riots (1875) and the Champaran Satyagraha (1917).

question: What is the major purpose of the Salal Dam located on Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hydroelectricity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Salal Dam" on the Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir was built mainly to generate hydroelectric power (hydroelectricity). It was India's first hydropower project on the Chenab. (सलाल बाँध — जलविद्युत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Salal project is a run-of-the-river scheme operated by the NHPC.

• The Chenab is one of the rivers allotted largely to Pakistan under the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), but India can use its waters for run-of-the-river power generation.

NOTE

• The Indus system consists of the Indus, Jhelum, Chenab (western rivers) and Ravi, Beas, Sutlej (eastern rivers). Other Chenab projects: Baglihar and Dulhasti.

question: Who amongst the following stated the Grameen model of microfinance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prof. Muhammad Yunus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Prof. Muhammad Yunus of Bangladesh developed the "Grameen model" of microfinance by founding the Grameen Bank, which provides small collateral-free loans to the poor (especially rural women). (ग्रामीण बैंक — मुहम्मद यूनुस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• For this pioneering work, Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

• Microfinance provides small loans, savings and insurance to low-income people who lack access to traditional banking.

NOTE

• Nobel context: Abhijit Banerjee won the 2019 Nobel in Economics (with Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer); Amartya Sen won the 1998 Nobel in Economics for welfare economics.

question: In February 2023, there have been protests in Punjab to release a group of Sikh prisoners who have been in jail for more than 30 years since militancy was wiped out in Punjab in the 1990s. What are these prisoners called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bandi Singhs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sikh prisoners who have remained in jail for more than 30 years (even after completing their sentences) since the era of militancy in Punjab are commonly referred to as "Bandi Singhs". Their release was a major demand during the February 2023 protests. (बंदी सिंह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Bandi" literally means prisoner/captive, and "Singh" is the surname adopted by Sikh men; hence "Bandi Singhs" = imprisoned Sikhs.

• The demand for their release has been raised by various Sikh religious and political bodies.

NOTE

• This topic falls under current affairs; SSC exams often ask about such terms that appear frequently in national news.

question: Who is the author of the book called 'Beneath the Surface: My Story'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Michael Phelps.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Beneath the Surface: My Story" is the autobiography of the American swimmer Michael Phelps, the most decorated Olympian of all time. (माइकल फेल्प्स की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Michael Phelps has won a record 28 Olympic medals, including 23 golds — more than any other athlete in history.

• He specialised in swimming (butterfly, freestyle and individual medley events).

NOTE

• Famous sports autobiographies: The Race of My Life (Milkha Singh), Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar) and Open (Andre Agassi).

question: The state religion of Bangladesh is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Islam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The state religion of Bangladesh is "Islam", though the constitution also guarantees the right to practise other religions. (बांग्लादेश का राजकीय धर्म — इस्लाम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bangladesh was created in 1971 after the Liberation War, separating from Pakistan; its capital is Dhaka and currency is the Bangladeshi Taka.

• The majority religion is Islam, with Hinduism being the largest minority faith.

NOTE

• India shares its longest international land border with Bangladesh (about 4,096 km). Bangladesh's national language is Bengali (Bangla).

question: Which of the following was authored by Harisenacharya?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brihatkatha Kosh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Brihatkatha Kosh (Brihat Katha Kosha)" was authored by Harishena (Harisenacharya), a Jain scholar. It is a Sanskrit work containing a collection of narrative/didactic Jain tales. (बृहत्कथा कोश — हरिषेणाचार्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Do not confuse this Harishena (the author) with the earlier Harishena, the court poet of Samudragupta, who composed the Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti).

• Note that Harishena's Brihatkatha Kosh is distinct from Gunadhya's famous Brihatkatha (in Paisachi Prakrit).

NOTE

• Rajatarangini was written by Kalhana (a history of Kashmir); Lilavati was written by the mathematician Bhaskara II (Bhaskaracharya).

question: Who among the following was 'Senani' in the Rig Vedic period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A war hero.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Rig Vedic period, "Senani" referred to the leader/commander of the army — a war hero (army general). The word comes from "Sena" (army). (सेनानी — सेनापति / युद्ध नायक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other Rig Vedic officials/terms: Rajan (king/chief), Purohita (chief priest), Gramani (head of a village), Vrajapati (officer in charge of pasture land).

• The two most important priests were Vasishtha and Vishwamitra.

NOTE

• The Rig Vedic society was tribal and pastoral; important popular assemblies were the Sabha and the Samiti, and cattle (Gau) were the main measure of wealth.

question: Which among the following is considered the first experiment of Satyagraha by Gandhiji in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Champaran.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Champaran Satyagraha (1917)" in Bihar was Mahatma Gandhi's first Satyagraha (experiment of Satyagraha) in India. It was launched to help indigo cultivators who were forced to grow indigo under the oppressive Tinkathia system. (चंपारण सत्याग्रह — 1917)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Kheda Satyagraha (1918) in Gujarat was for peasants unable to pay land revenue due to crop failure.

• The Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) was for the rights of textile mill workers.

• Gandhi first used the method of Satyagraha in South Africa against racial discrimination.

NOTE

• Champaran gave Gandhi his first major success in India and brought him national prominence in the freedom struggle.

question: Who became the first folk artist from India to walk the Cannes red carpet in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mame Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mame Khan, a renowned Rajasthani folk singer, became the first folk artist from India to walk the red carpet at the Cannes Film Festival in 2022. (मामे खान — कान फिल्म महोत्सव 2022)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He belongs to the Manganiyar community of Rajasthan, traditionally known for its folk music.

• He was part of the Indian delegation at Cannes 2022, where India was the "Country of Honour".

NOTE

• The Cannes Film Festival is held annually in Cannes, France; its top prize is the Palme d'Or (Golden Palm).

question: Sonal Mansingh is a famous proponent of which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sonal Mansingh is a celebrated Indian classical dancer, best known as a proponent of the Odissi dance form (she is also trained in Bharatanatyam). (सोनल मानसिंह — ओडिसी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• She was awarded the Padma Vibhushan and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

• Odissi is the classical dance form of Odisha, characterised by the tribhanga posture and graceful, fluid movements based on temple sculptures.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: The union list from the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution consists of how many subjects as of May 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hundred.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Union List of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains 100 subjects (as of May 2024), on which only the Parliament can make laws. (संघ सूची — 100 विषय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Originally the Union List had 97 subjects; the number has changed over time due to amendments.

• The State List currently has about 61 subjects and the Concurrent List about 52 subjects.

NOTE

• The Seventh Schedule (Article 246) divides powers into three lists: Union, State and Concurrent. Residuary powers (subjects not in any list) rest with the Union (Parliament).

question: Anita Sharma, Sangeet Natak Akademi Award winner, is an exponent of ________ dance form.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anita Sharma, a Sangeet Natak Akademi Award winner, is a noted exponent of the Sattriya dance form of Assam. (अनीता शर्मा — सत्रीया नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sattriya originated in the Vaishnava monasteries (Sattras) of Assam, introduced by the saint Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th century.

• It was recognised as a classical dance form by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

NOTE

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance and drama, established in 1952. Its highest honour is the Akademi Ratna (Fellowship).

question: In weight lifting, when an athlete misses all three attempts in the snatch or the clean and jerk, failing to post a total, it is known as _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombing-out.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In weightlifting, when a lifter misses all three attempts in either the snatch or the clean and jerk and therefore fails to record a valid total, it is called "bombing-out". (बॉम्बिंग-आउट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Competitive weightlifting has two lifts: the "snatch" and the "clean and jerk"; a lifter's total is the sum of the best successful lift in each.

• If a lifter "bombs out", they are ranked without a total and effectively out of medal contention.

NOTE

• Weightlifting is an Olympic sport governed by the International Weightlifting Federation (IWF). India's Mirabai Chanu won a silver medal in weightlifting at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics.

question:
Which of the following statements about Viharas is/are correct?

a) Viharas consist of a verandas, cell and hall around the walls of the hall.  b) Ajanta cave and Nashik cave are important parts of Vihara architecture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both a and b.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both statements are correct.

◦ (a) A "Vihara" (a Buddhist monastery/residence) typically consists of a central hall surrounded by small cells (rooms for monks) and a veranda.

◦ (b) The Ajanta caves (Maharashtra) and Nashik caves contain important examples of Vihara (monastery) architecture. (विहार — बौद्ध मठ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ancient Buddhist rock-cut architecture has two main types: the "Chaitya" (a prayer hall with a stupa) and the "Vihara" (a monastery/residence for monks).

• The Ajanta Caves are famous for their Buddhist paintings and murals and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Other important cave sites: Ellora (Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves), Karla, Bhaja and Kanheri. A place with many viharas came to be called a "Vihara" — the state name Bihar derives from it.

question: Which of the following phyla contains Leech?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Annelida.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Leech" belongs to the phylum "Annelida" — the segmented worms whose bodies are divided into ring-like segments (metameres). (जोंक — संघ ऐनेलिडा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Annelida includes earthworms, leeches and Nereis; these animals have a true coelom and a segmented (metameric) body.

• The leech (e.g., Hirudinaria) is an ectoparasite that sucks blood and secretes hirudin, an anticoagulant.

NOTE

• Quick recall: Platyhelminthes (flatworms, e.g., Planaria, tapeworm); Coelenterata/Cnidaria (Hydra, jellyfish); Nematoda (roundworms, e.g., Ascaris); Annelida (earthworm, leech).
